items.downgrade_reason: The skip_specs exception (set in .openspec.yaml) cannot be written as an applies_when predicate, so this is a should.

sources.quote: If the proposal lists no capabilities and `skip_specs` is not set, revisit the proposal first.
Delta operations (use ## headers): - **ADDED Requirements**: New capabilities - **MODIFIED Requirements**: ... - **REMOVED Requirements**: ... - **RENAMED Requirements**

items.note: Checking that a MODIFIED block is complete means comparing it with the main spec requirement it replaces. No kind does that comparison.

sources.quote: **MODIFIED Requirements**: Changed behavior - MUST include full updated content

items.note: Reason and Migration are required for each removed requirement, but only when a REMOVED section exists. No predicate can express that a section is present.

sources.quote: **REMOVED Requirements**: Deprecated features - MUST include **Reason** and **Migration**

items.note: The FROM:/TO: format applies only inside a RENAMED section. No predicate can express that a section is present.

sources.quote: **RENAMED Requirements**: Name changes only - use FROM:/TO: format
Each requirement: `### Requirement: <name>` followed by description

items.downgrade_reason: Only checks that SHALL/MUST appears somewhere. Whether every normative requirement uses it, and whether should/may is avoided, is not checked.

sources.quote: Use SHALL/MUST for normative requirements (avoid should/may)
Each scenario: `#### Scenario: <name>` with WHEN/THEN format
Each scenario: `#### Scenario: <name>` with WHEN/THEN format
`#### Scenario: <name>` ... **CRITICAL**: Scenarios MUST use exactly 4 hashtags (`####`). Using 3 hashtags or bullets will fail silently.

items.note: This needs a per-block check that each ### Requirement has a #### Scenario under it. item_format only counts lines across the whole file.

sources.quote: Every requirement MUST have at least one scenario.

items.note: This needs the length of each requirement's description, with existing MODIFIED blocks exempt. No generic kind measures text length.

sources.quote: Keep each requirement's description (the text between `### Requirement:` and its first scenario) to 500 characters or fewer.

items.note: Checking this means comparing each MODIFIED block with the existing main spec block as it was at BASE_SHA. No kind does that comparison.

sources.quote: Under MODIFIED, keep the existing requirement block whole; never split, trim or rewrite existing text just to meet the length.

items.note: Applies to each delta spec separately, only for capabilities with no main spec at BASE_SHA. It also requires Purpose to be the first section with at least 50 characters. Neither the per-capability condition nor the length can be expressed.

sources.quote: New capabilities only: the delta spec's first section is `## Purpose` - one or two sentences (50+ characters, or `openspec validate --strict` reports it as too brief)

items.note: Applies to each delta spec separately, only for capabilities whose main spec exists at BASE_SHA. Generic kinds cannot express that per-capability condition.

sources.quote: Do NOT add `## Purpose` to a delta for an existing capability - that spec already has one and the delta's is ignored.

unitemized.reason: Applies only when the user asks for a long requirement to be split. That condition cannot be observed or written as a predicate.
Applies only when the agent intends to change an existing capability's Purpose. That intent cannot be written as an applies_when predicate.
